Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement

Approved Uses of Biostimulators and Why the Breast Is Not One of Them

Approval is tied to a particular product, purpose and body area. That detail matters more than a broad claim that a product is approved.

Home/Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement/Biostimulators/Approved Uses of Biostimulators and Why the Breast Is Not One of Them

A product’s approval or registration is tied to a particular product, purpose and body area. This is a key part of assessing any offer made under the name of biostimulators.

Typical approved uses

Approvals vary by country, but commonly relate to facial applications such as deep lines, loss of facial volume, cheek contour or wrinkles. Some products also have medical uses for facial fat loss in specific conditions, or indications for hands or other areas. Check the current approval or registration for the exact product being proposed.

What is not typically approved

Breast enlargement or breast lift is generally not an approved use for these products. Using a product for that purpose is usually described as off-label.

What off-label means

Doctors may sometimes use products off-label based on their clinical judgement. It does not automatically make a use unsafe, but it means the regulator has not reviewed evidence for that specific purpose. Read more about approved and off-label use.

Why evidence matters

Results in the face do not predict results in the breast. Skin thickness, blood supply, movement and tissue type differ. A treatment that has a recognised facial indication may still have little evidence for a chest or breast use.

Questions to ask

  • Is this exact use approved or registered in India or elsewhere?
  • What evidence supports it in the chest or breast?
  • Why do you recommend it for me?
  • What will I be asked to sign for consent?

Red flags

  • Claims that a product is “FDA approved for breast enlargement”.
  • An unbranded or unclear product.
  • A refusal to show product documents or the batch details.

Key takeaway

Biostimulators have specific approved uses, and breast enlargement is not usually one of them.
